# fly_machine (Resource)

Manages a Fly.io machine. Supports create_before_destroy lifecycle.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "fly_machine" "web" {
  app    = fly_app.web.name
  name   = "web-1"
  region = "iad"
  image  = "registry.fly.io/my-app:latest"

  guest {
    cpu_kind  = "shared"
    cpus      = 1
    memory_mb = 512
  }

  env = {
    PORT = "8080"
  }

  # Activate secrets staged by fly_secret on this machine's next boot.
  min_secrets_version = fly_secret.database_url.version

  service {
    internal_port = 8080
    protocol      = "tcp"
    autostart     = true
    autostop      = "stop"

    port {
      port     = 443
      handlers = ["tls", "http"]
    }

    check {
      type     = "http"
      port     = 8080
      path     = "/health"
      interval = "10s"
      timeout  = "2s"
    }
  }

  mount {
    volume = fly_volume.data.id
    path   = "/data"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app` (String) Application name the machine belongs to.
- `image` (String) Docker image to run.

### Optional

- `check` (Block List) Machine-level health checks (the Machines API's `config.checks`). Create and Update block until every check reports `passing`, so a check here serializes a rolling apply: the next machine is not touched until this one is healthy. Use for machines that publish no `service` — a service's own `check` block is the right place otherwise, since it additionally gates Fly Proxy routing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--check))
- `container` (Block List) Additional container to co-run with the machine's main image (sidecar pattern). When at least one `container` block is declared, Fly's Machines API runs the top-level `image` as the first container and each `container` block as an additional container sharing the same firecracker microVM, network namespace, and `/.fly/api` socket.

Use this for tightly-coupled co-processes (e.g. an OTel Collector that scrapes the main service on `127.0.0.1`). Fly OIDC identity is per-machine, not per-container — every container on a machine is the same principal upstream. Never use a sidecar as an auth boundary. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--container))
- `desired_state` (String) State to converge the machine to after create/update: "started" (default) starts the machine and waits for checks; "stopped" stops it and skips check waits. Null behaves as "started". Use "stopped" to park a machine that has no services for Fly Proxy to manage.
- `env` (Map of String) Environment variables.
- `file` (Block List) Per-machine file written into the guest at create/update time. Exactly one of `raw_value` or `secret_name` must be set. This is how a cluster ships per-machine config (a Raft peer list, a node ID) without baking it into the image. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--file))
- `guest` (Block, Optional) Machine size configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--guest))
- `health_check_timeout` (String) Maximum time to wait for the health check (Go duration, default "60s").
- `health_check_url` (String) URL to poll after creation (e.g. "http://app.flycast:8081/health"). Machine is not marked created until this returns 200.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Machine metadata key/value pairs. The reserved `fly_process_group` key controls which `<group>.process.<app>.internal` 6PN DNS name resolves to this machine. Changes apply via UpdateMachine in-place (machine restart) — Fly's DNS picks up the new group without a fresh machine, confirmed by the feature owner.
- `metrics` (Block, Optional) Per-machine Prometheus scrape target. When set, Fly's managed Prometheus polls `http(s)://<machine-6pn>:<port><path>` every 15s and tags the resulting series with `app` / `instance` / `region` from the HOST machine's identity. Co-locate a sidecar that re-exposes the main service's metrics to get correct source attribution for free. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--metrics))
- `min_secrets_version` (Number) Minimum app secrets version the machine must be started with. Used to activate staged secrets on a new machine — set to the version returned by fly_secret.*.version.
- `mount` (Block List) Persistent volume mount. The referenced `fly_volume` must be in the same region AND on the same physical host as the machine — set the volume's `compute` block to match this machine's `guest` so Fly pre-places the volume on a compatible host.

Fly's Machines API does NOT support changing the `volume` of an existing mount in place ("you'll need to destroy the Machine and create a new one" per the docs). Plan-time enforcement would require RequiresReplace on a list-of-blocks which the framework doesn't model cleanly; a mid-apply API rejection is the fallback. To swap volumes, taint the machine.

Avoid `create_before_destroy` on a machine with mounts: Fly forbids two machines attaching to one volume, so the new machine's Create would fail the `validateMountsUnattached` guard while the old machine still holds the volume. The cluster bootstrap pattern (sequential, in-place replacement) is the supported flow. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--mount))
- `name` (String) Machine name. Used for idempotent creation. Immutable after create: Fly's Machines API accepts a `name` field in UpdateMachine but silently ignores it, so a post-create config change to `name` is absorbed with a warning rather than planned — importing a flyctl-deployed machine (auto-generated `weathered-frog-7982`) into a resource declaring `web-1` keeps the live name in state instead of forcing destroy+recreate. To genuinely rename, taint and recreate the machine.
- `region` (String) Fly.io region (e.g. "iad", "ord").
- `restart` (Block, Optional) Machine restart policy. Defaults to Fly's default ("on-failure" with 10 max retries) when unset. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--restart))
- `service` (Block List) Fly proxy service configuration. Required for Flycast routing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--service))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Machine ID.
- `image_digest` (String) SHA-256 digest of the running image.
- `instance_id` (String) Machine version ID. Changes on every update; used by the Wait API.
- `private_ip` (String) Internal 6PN address. May change if Fly migrates the machine.
- `state` (String) Current machine state (started, stopped, etc.).

<a id="nestedblock--check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `check`

Required:

- `name` (String) Check name. Becomes the key in the API's checks map, so it must be unique within the machine.
- `port` (Number) Port to check on the machine's 6PN address.
- `type` (String) Check type: "tcp" or "http".

Optional:

- `grace_period` (String) Time to wait after the machine starts before checking (e.g. "10s"). Covers boot time that would otherwise be reported as failure.
- `interval` (String) Time between checks (e.g. "10s").
- `method` (String) HTTP method. Only meaningful for type "http"; defaults to GET.
- `path` (String) HTTP path to request. Only meaningful for type "http".
- `timeout` (String) Maximum time a single check may take before it counts as failing (e.g. "5s").


<a id="nestedblock--container"></a>
### Nested Schema for `container`

Required:

- `image` (String) Docker image for this container.
- `name` (String) Container name within the machine. Must be unique per machine (Fly enforces); used in `depends_on.name` and surfaces in `flyctl logs --container <name>`.

Optional:

- `cmd` (List of String) Override the image's default CMD (argv tail).
- `depends_on` (Block List) Ordering constraints — this container starts only after every named dependency reaches the requested condition. The named container must also be declared on this machine. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--container--depends_on))
- `entrypoint` (List of String) Override the image's default ENTRYPOINT (argv head).
- `env` (Map of String) Environment variables scoped to this container only. Merged with the machine-level `env` at runtime (container-level wins on collision).
- `file` (Block List) Per-container files written into the container's filesystem at create/update time. Same semantics as the machine-level `file` block but scoped to this container only (so a sidecar's config doesn't leak into the main container's image). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--container--file))
- `healthcheck` (Block List) Per-container health check. A readiness check here is what makes another container's `depends_on { condition = "healthy" }` resolve; the machine-level `check` block does not satisfy it — a machine check reaching `passing` leaves the gated container unstarted with no error and no event.

Exposes `tcp`, `http` and `exec`, exactly one per block. Two API fields are deliberately absent rather than missing: `headers` on an http check (a header on a health probe is normally a credential, and there is no secret reference for one — it would sit in plaintext HCL and in state), and `unhealthy` (the API's only value is "stop", so the knob would have one setting). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--container--healthcheck))
- `restart` (Block, Optional) Container-level restart policy. Inherits the machine policy when unset. "spot-price" is not supported at the container level. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--container--restart))
- `secret` (Block List) Inject an app-level fly_secret into this container as an env var. Use when a sidecar needs a per-machine secret — define one secret per machine with a unique name (`API_KEY_REPLICA_<N>`) and use this block to rename it to the same env var (`API_KEY`) inside every container. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--container--secret))

<a id="nestedblock--container--depends_on"></a>
### Nested Schema for `container.depends_on`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of another container on this machine that this container depends on.

Optional:

- `condition` (String) Required dependency state: "started", "healthy", or "exited_successfully".


<a id="nestedblock--container--file"></a>
### Nested Schema for `container.file`

Required:

- `guest_path` (String) Absolute path inside the container where the file is written.

Optional:

- `mode` (Number) File mode bits.
- `raw_value` (String) Base64-encoded file contents.
- `secret_name` (String) Name of an app secret whose value is the base64-encoded file contents.


<a id="nestedblock--container--healthcheck"></a>
### Nested Schema for `container.healthcheck`

Required:

- `name` (String) Check name. Must be unique within the container.

Optional:

- `exec` (Attributes) Command check: the container is healthy while the command exits 0. The command runs inside this container, so its image has to contain it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--container--healthcheck--exec))
- `failure_threshold` (Number) Consecutive failures before the container counts as unhealthy.
- `grace_period_seconds` (Number) Seconds to wait after the container starts before checking. Covers boot time that would otherwise be reported as failure.
- `http` (Attributes) HTTP request check. Use for a service that listens before it is ready to serve, where a TCP connect would report healthy too early. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--container--healthcheck--http))
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Seconds between checks. Seconds, not a duration string — the machine-level `check` block's `interval` is the duration-string one.
- `kind` (String) Check kind: "readiness" or "liveness". Use "readiness" for a check that another container's `depends_on { condition = "healthy" }` should wait on.
- `success_threshold` (Number) Consecutive successes before the container counts as healthy.
- `tcp` (Attributes) TCP connect check: the container is healthy while the port accepts a connection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--container--healthcheck--tcp))
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Seconds a single check may take before it counts as failing.

<a id="nestedatt--container--healthcheck--exec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `container.healthcheck.exec`

Required:

- `command` (List of String) Command and arguments, e.g. ["vault", "status"]. An argv list, not a shell line — use ["/bin/sh", "-c", "..."] when you need shell semantics.


<a id="nestedatt--container--healthcheck--http"></a>
### Nested Schema for `container.healthcheck.http`

Required:

- `port` (Number) Port to check.

Optional:

- `method` (String) HTTP method. Defaults to Fly's default (GET) when unset.
- `path` (String) Path to request.
- `scheme` (String) "http" or "https". Defaults to Fly's default (http) when unset.
- `tls_server_name` (String) Hostname to validate the TLS certificate against. Only meaningful when scheme is "https".
- `tls_skip_verify` (Boolean) Skip TLS certificate validation. Only meaningful when scheme is "https"; the usual case is a health endpoint behind a self-signed certificate on loopback.


<a id="nestedatt--container--healthcheck--tcp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `container.healthcheck.tcp`

Required:

- `port` (Number) Port to check.



<a id="nestedblock--container--restart"></a>
### Nested Schema for `container.restart`

Optional:

- `max_retries` (Number) Maximum restart attempts when policy is "on-failure".
- `policy` (String) Restart policy: "no", "always", or "on-failure".


<a id="nestedblock--container--secret"></a>
### Nested Schema for `container.secret`

Required:

- `env_var` (String) Name of the env var inside the container.

Optional:

- `name` (String) Source secret name (must match a fly_secret on the app). Omit to use the same name as env_var.



<a id="nestedblock--file"></a>
### Nested Schema for `file`

Required:

- `guest_path` (String) Absolute path inside the guest where the file is written (e.g. "/etc/clickhouse-keeper/keeper_config.xml").

Optional:

- `mode` (Number) File mode bits (chmod(2)). Defaults to Fly's default (0644).
- `raw_value` (String) Base64-encoded file contents. Use `base64encode(templatefile(...))` in HCL. Mutually exclusive with `secret_name`.
- `secret_name` (String) Name of an app secret whose value is the base64-encoded file contents. Mutually exclusive with `raw_value`.


<a id="nestedblock--guest"></a>
### Nested Schema for `guest`

Optional:

- `cpu_kind` (String) CPU kind: "shared" or "performance".
- `cpus` (Number) Number of CPUs.
- `memory_mb` (Number) Memory in megabytes.


<a id="nestedblock--metrics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metrics`

Optional:

- `https` (Boolean) Use https instead of http. Defaults to false.
- `path` (String) URL path to scrape. Defaults to Fly's default ("/metrics") when unset.
- `port` (Number) Port the Fly scraper connects to on the machine's 6PN address.


<a id="nestedblock--mount"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mount`

Required:

- `path` (String) Absolute mount path inside the guest (e.g. "/var/lib/clickhouse-keeper").
- `volume` (String) Volume ID to attach (the `id` attribute of a `fly_volume` resource). Cannot be changed in place — taint the machine to swap volumes.

Optional:

- `name` (String) Optional display name for the mount. Defaults to the volume's name.
- `readopt_on_host_migration` (Boolean) When true, `Read` reconciles this mount's `volume` from the live machine so a Fly host migration (which forks the volume to a new ID and re-mounts it) surfaces as state drift instead of staying invisible. Set this ONLY in tandem with `readopt_on_host_migration = true` on the paired `fly_volume`: the volume resource re-anchors its `id` to the fork on the same refresh, so config (`mount.volume = fly_volume.id`) and the refreshed mount agree on the new ID and no illegal in-place volume swap is planned. If this were on while the paired volume stayed on the old ID (flag off, or an ambiguous re-anchor decline), the mount would move to the fork while config still pointed at the orphan — producing exactly the mid-apply `UpdateMachine` volume-swap Fly rejects. Defaults to false, which preserves the prior behavior (mounts are never read back) for every machine that doesn't opt in.


<a id="nestedblock--restart"></a>
### Nested Schema for `restart`

Optional:

- `max_retries` (Number) Maximum restart attempts when policy is "on-failure". Ignored for other policies.
- `policy` (String) Restart policy: "no", "always", "on-failure", or "spot-price".


<a id="nestedblock--service"></a>
### Nested Schema for `service`

Required:

- `internal_port` (Number) Port the application listens on.

Optional:

- `autostart` (Boolean) Automatically start machine on incoming request.
- `autostop` (String) Autostop behavior: "off", "stop", or "suspend".
- `check` (Block List) Health check configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--service--check))
- `concurrency` (Block List) Fly Proxy load-balancing thresholds for this service (at most one block). When present, all three attributes are required; omit the block entirely to leave Fly's defaults. Modeled as a size-1 list rather than a single block so it is genuinely optional — a single nested block would enforce its required attributes even when omitted. Use `type = "connections"` for a service holding long-lived connections such as WebSockets, so the proxy counts open sockets — it wakes another machine at `soft_limit` and stops routing new connections at `hard_limit`. Like the rest of the `service` block, these values are write-only: they are never read back from the Machines API into state, so Terraform will not detect a server-side clamp or coercion of the limits as drift. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--service--concurrency))
- `port` (Block List) Port handler configuration for Fly proxy routing (Flycast). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--service--port))
- `protocol` (String) Protocol: "tcp" or "udp".

<a id="nestedblock--service--check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `service.check`

Required:

- `type` (String) Check type: "tcp" or "http".

Optional:

- `interval` (String) Check interval (e.g. "10s").
- `method` (String) HTTP method (e.g. "GET").
- `path` (String) HTTP path to check.
- `port` (Number) Port to check.
- `timeout` (String) Check timeout (e.g. "2s").


<a id="nestedblock--service--concurrency"></a>
### Nested Schema for `service.concurrency`

Required:

- `hard_limit` (Number) Count at which the proxy stops routing new connections to this machine.
- `soft_limit` (Number) Count at which the proxy starts spilling load to (and waking) another pool machine.
- `type` (String) What the proxy counts: "connections" (persistent sockets) or "requests". Set explicitly — see concurrencyModel for why this stays Required rather than Optional+Computed.


<a id="nestedblock--service--port"></a>
### Nested Schema for `service.port`

Required:

- `port` (Number) Port number the proxy listens on.

Optional:

- `handlers` (List of String) Protocol handlers (e.g. ["http"]).
